entry.title: The Art of Model Orchestration: Building RouteLLM
entry.summary:
In the current AI landscape, we often treat LLMs as monoliths. We send a simple "Hello" to the same GPT-4o that handles our complex architectural reviews. This is inefficient. This is expensive. RouteLLM is my attempt to visualize the solution: Intelligent Model Routing. Cloud LLMs are powerful but come with three major drawbacks: Latency: Even the fastest cloud models have round-trip times. Cost: Token pricing adds up at scale. Data Privacy: Not every prompt should leave your local edge. The core of RouteLLM is its Simulation Engine. It mimics how a production orchestrator evaluates "Complexity" vs "Cost". const chosenModel = complexity > 65 ? 'cloud' : 'local';

entry.title: Have Developers Lost The Spark
entry.summary: I've changed my mind about DSA's, you've heard it every where - "leetcode is dying", "You don't need to know DSA, AI is here" While I am a big fan of new technologies, I also like to know what I am doing and what my code is doing, that doesn't just give me peace of mind it it saves me time when I am debugging, I don't know about you but I feel lost when I use AI to change a lot of my code Recently I've been reading more code then actually writing, diving into DSA problems, and even had to refresh my knowledge about Big O notation and more. I really enjoy it and I feel like as devs we have forgotten how to enjoy the process and now see code as means to an end or something like that... Personally I find joy in it and I am pretty sure I am not the only one. The tools and frameworks didn't make us developers...our curiosity, problem solving, the drive to build, break fix and innovate did + nerding out over computers, Cheers
